name: Bloodmage: Blood Shield keeps health regeneration running in combat at 150% of the normal rate, and nothing regenerates in combat without it (#362)
contract: Blood Shield 504296 (Spell.dbc, family 26, class 20 grant at level 4): effect 1 is aura 88 SPELL_AURA_MOD_HEALTH_REGEN_PERCENT with BasePoints 49 + DieSides 1 = 50, effect 2 is aura 116 SPELL_AURA_MOD_REGEN_DURING_COMBAT with value 100; tooltip 'Your health regeneration now continues in combat and is increased by 50%'. No other spell a level-5 Bloodmage owns carries a health-regeneration aura, and the in-combat measurement uses a passive fixture that never swings back, so health moves only by regeneration. Expected: out of combat without the shield the Bloodmage regenerates its normal rate R per 2 s tick; in combat without the shield it regenerates nothing; in combat with the shield it regenerates 1.5 R per tick. Each window starts about 1 s after an observed tick and lasts 20 s, so it holds exactly 10 ticks; Player::RegenerateHealth truncates each tick to an integer, so the in-combat/out-of-combat ratio lies in 1.35-1.75 for any per-tick base above 7 health (a level-5 Bloodmage has about 27 Spirit and the CoA client's gtOCTRegenHP custom-class row 0.274 at level 5). The ratio is independent of Rate.Health and EnableLowLevelRegenBoost, which scale both windows alike. It rejects in-combat regeneration without the shield, a shield that only restores the unboosted rate (1.0) and a doubled bonus (2.0 or more). The absolute rate stays recorded, not asserted: no independent source states the intended Bloodmage regeneration magnitude. The maximum health is fixed at 5000 so no window reaches the cap.
